text:
Boston spent two periods and most of a third hitting a wall, then walked through it in 75 seconds. Fraser Minten snapped one home at 16:14 of the third to break a scoreless game, JJ Peterka matched him at 17:06, and Mark Kastelic closed it at 17:29. Three even-strength goals in the last four minutes turned a tight, grinding game into a 3-0 BOS win over NYR.

The decisive stretch was the product of a period Boston had owned. The Bruins generated 1.78 expected goals in the third to the Rangers' 0.71, after the first two periods were close to even (0.63 to 0.37 in the first, 0.97 to 0.93 in the second). Across the game BOS led 3.38 to 2.01 in expected goals and 55 to 47 in shot attempts, which is why a simulation of every shot gives Boston the win 61 percent of the time. Kastelic's goal was the one real gift: a 76 percent chance, by far the best look of the night. Minten and Peterka scored on 10 and 15 percent chances, the kind of finishes that rarely come in bunches.

The reason it stayed scoreless so long was Jeremy Swayman, who stopped all 24 shots and faced 2.01 expected goals, saving about two more than an average goalie would have. Igor Shesterkin was good too, but the margin between the goalies was the margin in the game. Minten finished with a goal, an assist and a hand in two of the three scores, and Hampus Lindholm's 2.02 expected goals for while he was on the ice led all Bruins skaters.
